drift.note: Superseded in v1.2: weights do not drift by counting behavior. Only Personality drifts, per the personality.drift rules above. The old weight-drift table is removed, not kept as an alternative.

meanings.w_goal: How close this action gets the entity to its current goal (e.g. a hunter's goal 'catch prey today' makes hunting score high).
meanings.w_memory: Whether memory pushes toward or away from this action (attacked by someone -> revenge / avoidance scores high; helped by someone -> helping them scores high).
meanings.w_need: How urgently this action relieves a need (hunger 90 -> eating scores near 1; hunger 10 -> eating scores low).
meanings.w_reputation: How this action affects reputation (helping a friendly faction scores high; offending one scores low).
meanings.w_schedule: Whether it is the right time for this action (working at the forge by day scores high; at midnight it scores low).
meanings.w_personality: How well this action matches the entity's Personality component (bravery, aggression, curiosity, greed, sociability, caution). This is the root-cause term: behavior is the result, not the cause.

score: score(action) = w_need * need(action) + w_memory * memory(action) + w_reputation * reputation(action) + w_goal * goal(action) + w_schedule * schedule(action) + w_personality * personality(action). Each term is normalized to 0..1 before weighting.

personality.component: Personality { bravery, aggression, curiosity, greed, sociability, caution }, each 0-10, initial values in creature data

drift.note: Personality drifts slowly and only after major events, never by counting how often an action was done. Counting behavior is circular: the trait is the cause, the behavior is the result.

personality.note: Player and NPC share the same rule. A player's Personality is set at character creation (data, player-chosen or random) and drifts by the same major-event rules; offline takeover uses that same Personality, so offline behavior mirrors the player's own traits.
